definitions.explanation: Rigorous training to master a skill or art.
Spiritual discipline practiced in Buddhism and other religions.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}の{修行|しゅぎょう}をする。
{修行|しゅぎょう}{時代|じだい}は{厳|きび}しかった。
10{年|ねん}の{修行|しゅぎょう}を{経|へ}て、やっと{一人前|いちにんまえ}の{職人|しょくにん}になった。
examples.english: After ten years of training, I finally became a full-fledged craftsman.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}で{修行|しゅぎょう}する{僧侶|そうりょ}。
examples.english: A monk training in the mountains.

examples.japanese: {厳|きび}しい{修行|しゅぎょう}に{耐|た}える。
お{寺|てら}で{座禅|ざぜん}の{修行|しゅぎょう}をして、{心|こころ}が{落|お}ち{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: I did Zen meditation practice at a temple and felt at peace.

notes:
{修行|しゅぎょう} refers to rigorous, sustained training — either for mastering a professional skill or for spiritual discipline. It implies dedication and perseverance beyond casual practice.

TWO MAIN CONTEXTS:
1. Professional: Apprenticeship-style training to master a craft ({料理|りょうり}の{修行|しゅぎょう} — culinary training)
2. Religious: Ascetic or meditative practice in Buddhism ({座禅|ざぜん}の{修行|しゅぎょう} — Zen meditation practice)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {修行|しゅぎょう}する: to undergo training/discipline
- {修行|しゅぎょう}{中|ちゅう}: in training, undergoing practice
- {修行|しゅぎょう}{時代|じだい}: training period/apprenticeship years
- {武者|むしゃ}{修行|しゅぎょう}: warrior's training journey (also used figuratively)
- {修行|しゅぎょう}{僧|そう}: ascetic monk

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {修行|しゅぎょう}: rigorous training (professional or spiritual)
- {練習|れんしゅう}: practice (everyday, routine)
- {訓練|くんれん}: training (systematic, often physical or military)
- {修業|しゅうぎょう}: study/training to complete a course (different kanji, similar meaning)
